summary: Phase 3 A green gate independent of active-track Red accepted. The new `npm run test:shipped` script (wired to scripts/test-shipped.mjs) is the canonical shipped-surface green gate, fully independent of the active track's four S1 intentional-Red files and of `npm run parity`. lib/green-gate.mjs#partitionTests is exact-name matching (Set.has) over four candidate path forms — bare English words like 'red' or 'skip' are not filters — and produces byte-identical results across repeated calls. scripts/test-shipped.mjs reads tests/.track-red-files.txt correctly (comment lines, blank lines, and whitespace all filtered) and emits the explicit partition listing `[shipped] running N test files: ...; [track-red] excluded M: ...; [unclassified] U: ...`. Against the live repo at current HEAD f914e2b, partitionTests returns exactly 5 shipped (core, green-gate, model-resolution, parity, setup), 4 trackRed (agents-snapshot, grammar, manifest, preflight), and 0 unclassified. `node scripts/test-shipped.mjs` exits 0 with all 37 shipped assertions passing (5 files × tests: core=5, green-gate=8, model-resolution=9, parity=11, setup=4); `npm test` exits 1 with EXACTLY 4 failures (the documented S1 intentional-Red files). package.json was modified by an additive single-line change that introduces `test:shipped` while leaving the existing `test`, `check`, `parity`, `configure`, `migrate-auth` and other scripts untouched. Phase 1 (parity 11/11) and Phase 2 (model-resolution 9/9, core 5/5) show no regression. Red falsification at intermediate Red commit b0d3e59 is recorded in phase-3-red.json (node --test tests/green-gate.test.mjs exit 1, 0/8 pass). The Node v22.22.3 recursive-test compatibility adapter in lib/green-gate.mjs is a narrowly scoped, opt-in shim that only fires when a child `node --test` is invoked with exactly two argv entries (a single test file); the production gate passes 5 files so this adapter does not fire on the production invocation path. plan.md still carries `[ ]` pending markers per the strategy §3 compatibility marker grammar; the supervisor's migration is the owner of that state, not a Phase 3 gate, and the strategy explicitly accepts this state. The phase-3 role-gate mechanical check is permitted and was run; its FAIL lines are all accounted for as expected/non-blocking (audit-only role = phase-acceptance requires canonical role unavailable due to openai-codex OAuth failure; nonblocking_findings list-of-objects format mismatch in phase-3-review-c.json payload; audit-only role changed worktree status outside its result artifact = pre-existing dirty tree; current phase has 9 [ ] markers = explicitly accepted per strategy §3; missing prerequisite result for review-a/review-b/adversarial-testing/ux-browser-review = those roles never ran due to openai-codex OAuth failure, user-authorized substitution by measure-final-acceptance). None block Phase 3 acceptance. All three implementation phases accepted; the track's review-c (C1) and final-acceptance may proceed.
